newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends touch higher ahead of LME data.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends touch higher ahead of LME data.

text.p: COMEX copper settled slightly firmer as the market kept within the higher range set last week, propped up by a stronger LME cash to three months premium.

"Supply side in the long-term is going to weigh on the market, but right now we continue to benefit from the strong spreads," said William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch. "This is going to continue carrying prices higher."
The LME premium rose some $30 since Friday to $180/$190, with particular tightness in the cash to February spread.
The next LME stock report is due Tuesday and traders forecasts ranged from a 2,000-tonne drop to a hike of 9,000 tonnes.
March COMEX copper settled 0.25 cent firmer at 106.35 cents per pound, traded 107.35 to 105.80 cents. Spot January went out 0.80 cent higher at 109.30 cents.
The International Copper Study Group said there was a refined metal surplus of 65,000 tonnes at the end of October 1996 compared to a deficit of 469,000 tonnes in the same month in 1995.
And Chile's mining minister Benjamin Teplizky said the country's copper production will rise to 3.39 million tonnes this year and to 4.4 million in 1999, compared to 3.07 million last year.
Meanwhile no date has been fixed for further labor talks at Phelps Dodge's Chino mine in New Mexico where workers have been without a contract for over six months.
A Phelps Dodge spokeswoman said the mine was still operating normally. A United Steelworkers of America official said both sides were corresponding to fix further meetings.
